design_rationale:
TASK 1 DOSSIER (prime_enrollment_fees_and_pcm, M=2). Worklog kept from Step 0; reworked in rounds 2-5 after the policy-task audits.

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed: {"task": 1, "key": "env_0055_military_health_plan_administrator/prime_enrollment_fees_and_pcm/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 4, 4]}. The supplement carries 5 factors; the credit, the refund and the initial payment carry 4 each.

[Why this is a good test] Raymond asks for one thing - to pay up his new Prime enrollment with a one-time payment from his checking account. The agent must discover from the initial-payment policy's prerequisite sentences that (1) the new enrollment's first installment is not fully charged - a late application stretches it through October, August, which Select coverage also touched, is billed less Select's monthly share, and the October installment the region already billed counts against it, leaving September uncharged; (2) the first installment was paid twice - a card payment at sign-up and a bank bill-pay two days later - and the transfer made outside the card arrangement must be refunded, less the one regular installment the region keeps on the account because the card has collected; and (3) the Prime enrollment he ended in April must first stand credited for April, which his Select coverage reached from the day after he left Prime, although the disenrollment credit covered only May and June. Each write is a multi-factor computation over two Prime accounts and the Select records. Difficulty comes from reading rules and reconciling ledgers, never from picking among similar tools: each hidden tool is named by exactly one policy.

[Scope - occupied / claimed] Task 0 occupies prime_ext_reinstatement_catch_up, prime_ext_duplicate_payment_refund (an applied or active enrollment's duplicate on an installment other than its first installment charge; where its selection lands on the first installment charge of an enrollment that took effect in the current plan year it refunds nothing, that duplicate being this task's), prime_ext_current_installment_payment and prime_ext_draft_on_file_method with their four tools. Task 1 claims the four remaining policies and tools: prime_ext_unused_month_credit (post_unused_month_credit_3ad1a050), prime_ext_first_installment_duplicate_refund (refund_first_installment_duplicate_7d2e91c4), prime_ext_first_installment_supplement (post_first_installment_supplement_bc87e2fc) and prime_ext_initial_payment (pay_first_installment_by_bank_draft_5f63627f, owner=user). The duplicate on the new enrollment's first installment belongs to prime_ext_first_installment_duplicate_refund, whose scope is the first installment, paid more than once, of an enrollment that took effect in the current plan year (Raymond's took effect 2026-08-24); no policy or tool is shared. The charter splits enrollments by the plan year they took effect in, so every prerequisite state has exactly one policy that can bring it about: the catch-up, the draft and the one-time payment act only on an enrollment that took effect before the current plan year; the first-installment supplement, the first-installment duplicate refund and the initial payment act only on one that took effect in the current plan year; the duplicate refund leaves the first installment of a current-plan-year enrollment to the first-installment duplicate refund. Raymond's new enrollment took effect 2026-08-24, so the supplement, the first-installment duplicate refund and the initial payment act on it, while the catch-up, the draft, the one-time payment and the duplicate refund's claim on its first installment would figure nothing on it.

[Problem-tree card] Root: prime_ext_initial_payment (on_request; the customer's surface request; owner=user tool). Prerequisite problems: prime_ext_first_installment_supplement (state_due), prime_ext_first_installment_duplicate_refund (state_due), prime_ext_unused_month_credit (state_due). Fan-out; topological order prime_ext_unused_month_credit -> prime_ext_first_installment_duplicate_refund -> prime_ext_first_installment_supplement -> prime_ext_initial_payment (the three prerequisites commute).
 Edge 1 prime_ext_initial_payment<-prime_ext_first_installment_supplement: value_input, gate rp_owed, form state. Sentence: "An initial payment toward a new enrollment is figured only after the enrollment's installment charges cover every month from the month containing its effective date through the last month its first installment owes." Connective "only after"; record-visible state (months inside installment charges' coverage); names no action, performer or tool; false at frozen time (September uncharged).
 Edge 2 prime_ext_initial_payment<-prime_ext_first_installment_duplicate_refund: value_input, gate rp_returned, form state. Sentence: "An initial payment toward a new enrollment is figured only after its first installment carries no payments beyond its value other than what the region keeps on the account for the installments that follow." Connective "only after"; record-visible state (payments against the first installment less refunds against them, beside its value and what the region keeps); false at frozen time (57.49 beyond the 32.51 value against 32.51 kept).
 Edge 3 prime_ext_initial_payment<-prime_ext_unused_month_credit: state_gate, gate prime_fee_ledger.coverage_period_start, form state. Sentence: "An initial payment toward a new Prime enrollment is not taken until every month of the last paid installment of a Prime enrollment the beneficiary ended earlier in the same plan year that a following TRICARE Select enrollment's coverage reaches, or that falls after the month containing its disenrollment date, stands credited." Connective "not ... until"; the state is months inside a credit's coverage period; false at frozen time (April uncredited). The condition reads Select coverage from the Select enrollment dates, as the sentence and the credit rule do.
 Value-input edges 2 of 3 (floor 2). Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skip credit -> payment 48.52 with the state gate unmet; skip duplicate refund -> payment 32.51; skip supplement -> payment 32.51. The tool layer validates none of these.

[Factor card] (tier taken -> figure; baseline figure in brackets). The monthly rate is not a factor: it is one twelfth of the annual fee of the enrollment's recorded fee arrangement (individual, 390.12 -> 32.51), as the base fee schedule sets it.
 Credit (expected 32.51, all-baseline 16.26): counting from April, Select coverage reaching every Q2 month (cross-difficulty select) [0.0]; month value one third of the quarterly charge [0.0]; April at the full value, Select taking effect the next day (multi-source, cross-difficulty select) [0.0]; the 65.02 credit already posted comes off [97.53].
 Duplicate refund (expected 24.98, all-baseline 0.0): first installment valued at one twelfth, being monthly [0.0]; the latest 70.00 transfer, made outside the card arrangement, returned [20.0]; a regular installment kept valued by the monthly October installment [0.0]; one regular installment kept, the card having collected (multi-source) [57.49].
 Supplement (expected 16.01, all-baseline 0.0): last month October, late application [0.0]; August whole, a qualifying-life-event enrollment [0.0]; Select coverage touches August (cross-difficulty select) [32.51]; Select's share one third of its quarterly installment (cross-difficulty select) [28.39]; every charge on the account counts, one having been posted after the application [48.52].
 Initial payment (expected 48.52, all-baseline 0.0): charges settled August-October 81.03 [32.51]; the card not yet started, counted after the application month [16.01]; one installment ahead, recurring card with nothing billed past October (multi-source) [16.01]; valued at one twelfth [406.13].
 Baselines are the plain fee-desk methods: on a plain account (first installment paid once, nothing overpaid, nothing billed late) the duplicate refund is 0.00 and the initial payment is the open installment, which the scratch harness synth.py confirms.
 Per-task floors: multi-source factors credit_switch_month_value (the Select effective date against the Prime disenrollment date), first_duplicate_amount_kept (the arrangement's method with the ledger's collections) and initial_months_ahead (the arrangement's method with the ledger's collections and latest coverage); cross-difficulty factors credit_months_counted, credit_switch_month_value, supplement_select_coverage and supplement_select_share (select). Every tier is decided from ledger aggregates, dates or the Select records; the enrollment fields read are the arrangement's frequency and method and the enrollment reason, none of which names an outcome.

[Base-invariant card] Credit (prime_fee_credit): prime_fee_proration_credit.credit_against_paid_installment - "A credit is posted only against an installment charge that has a payment posted against it." - the Q2 charge carries the 97.53 card payment; overwrites declared for 'the month in which the disenrollment date falls is never credited' and 'once per installment and reason'. The April credit leaves the ended enrollment with a 32.51 credit balance, which the unchanged base clause refunds through the original card within fee_refund_issue_days (30 for Retiree Group A); that refund belongs to the region's refund cycle, no tool in this task issues it and no gold action reads it. Duplicate refund (prime_fee_refund): prime_fee_proration_credit scope only; overwrite declared for the refund-of-credit-balance clause within its own scope (the region keeps regular installments of a first-installment overpayment on the account). Supplement (prime_fee_charge): prime_enrollment_fee_schedule.fee_bearing_enrollment_open - "Installments are charged only on a fee-bearing enrollment whose status is applied or active." - the new enrollment is active and fee-bearing; overwrite declared for the first-installment clause. Initial payment (prime_fee_payment): prime_fee_payment_methods.method_allowed_for_frequency - a one-time bank draft is accepted for monthly installments of Group A - and prime_nonpayment_disenrollment scope; overwrite declared for 'never to a future period' (an installment paid ahead).

[Business-object card] Holdings: the ended enrollment 1fca7e50-6e23-4480-a430-0bfe9abe5b8f (credit) and the new enrollment de31d535-2465-460f-8bc3-71470707f52c (duplicate refund, supplement and payment); one customer c44b9b16-02c7-45e2-b6c6-83573b659622; one Select enrollment d7ebac6f-dbfc-4079-8a3c-69bbd49af046. Credit against the Q2 charge b84c95e6-57b3-446d-b8f5-6a8361e3a11a; refund against the 70.00 bill-pay transfer 6f39c047-21fc-48af-acc9-e6b4d65af6c9 on the first installment 2489efda-053d-4c9f-91a7-7d74473657bc; supplement created at step 13 on de31d535-2465-460f-8bc3-71470707f52c; payment against the October installment c763ef83-9fda-4000-9edb-e2a53d014bd6.

[Seed design] One customer (single enrollee: one customer lookup is allowed), two DEERS moves (2026-04-17 to Elko, 2026-08-24 back to Las Vegas), two Prime enrollments, one Select enrollment, 18 Prime ledger rows (2025 Q1-Q4 and 2026 Q1-Q2 quarterly charges with card payments, the May-June credit and its refund; the new first installment with its 20.00 sign-up card payment and 70.00 bill-pay transfer, and the October installment posted 2026-10-07) and 6 Select ledger rows. Balances equal ledger sums (0.00 and -24.98). All rows are states the charters produce; every row is read by the gold reads.

[Persona design] Raymond is businesslike; he volunteers the surface request and the background he knows. Identity details only when asked; payments only when asked and without amounts; passive acceptance of the old enrollment being settled first and of money going back to his bank account or card; completes the payment step exactly as handed; ends when the payment goes through, which is the last gold action.

[Traps] (a) Taking the payment on the August charge alone without the supplement. (b) Supplementing September and October although October is already billed, missing the netting of Select's August share, or prorating August by days although the enrollment rests on a qualifying life event. (c) Ignoring the ended enrollment's uncredited April, crediting it at one twelfth of the quarterly charge or at nothing, or crediting the whole quarter without taking off the 65.02 already credited. (d) Refunding the whole 57.49 excess or the whole 70.00 transfer, keeping nothing on the account although the card has collected, or returning the 20.00 card payment instead of the transfer made outside the arrangement. (e) Forgetting the installment paid ahead while the card has not started, or treating the 20.00 sign-up card payment as the card having started. (f) Netting the refund out of the payment instead of owing it again.

[Standard solution] Locate by DBN, verify (DBN, DOB, SSN last four), read both Prime enrollments and their ledgers, the Select enrollment and ledger, DEERS events; post the April credit 32.51 (2026-04-01..2026-04-30, beneficiary_disenrollment) against Q2; refund 24.98 against the 70.00 bill-pay transfer; post the supplement 16.01 (2026-09-01..2026-09-30); hand Raymond the one-time bank draft of 48.52 against the October installment.

[Verification] Scratch scripts in /tmp/erl55_prime (build_t1v2_core.py, sim1v2.py, eval1v2.py, synth.py) replay gold with the real share and task tools and evaluate each policy's compute with the gate sandbox at its handling time: credit 32.51, duplicate refund 24.98, supplement 16.01, initial payment 48.52; every factor's baseline gives a different figure; the six orders of the three prerequisites give the same values and terminal hash.

[Closure] policy -> tool -> computation step -> GT call: prime_ext_unused_month_credit -> post_unused_month_credit_3ad1a050 -> step 9; prime_ext_first_installment_duplicate_refund -> refund_first_installment_duplicate_7d2e91c4 -> step 11; prime_ext_first_installment_supplement -> post_first_installment_supplement_bc87e2fc -> step 13; prime_ext_initial_payment -> pay_first_installment_by_bank_draft_5f63627f -> step 15 (user). required_documents equal charter_scope.extended_policies.
user_scenario: You are Raymond D. Teague, 51, a retired Army sergeant first class living in Las Vegas; you are friendly and businesslike and you like to get things finished in one call. In April you took a job up in Elko, so you dropped your TRICARE Prime the day before you moved and went onto TRICARE Select. In late August you moved back to Las Vegas, cancelled Select the day before the move, and on October 6 you signed back up for Prime, which the office told you would start back on the date of your move; you set the new enrollment up to be paid by your card each month. That is why you are calling: you want to pay whatever you owe on your new Prime enrollment so that it is fully paid up, with a one-time payment from your checking account, and you would like it done on this call. You do not know how much you owe, how the region figures it, or how your account is set up beyond the fact that your card pays it each month; you never name an amount yourself. When the agent asks who you are, you give your DoD Benefits Number, 11010274631, and when asked for more you give your date of birth as 1975-02-14 and the last four of your Social Security number, 1846. If asked for anything else on file, your phone number is 2535551362, your email is raymond.teague.lv@gmail.com and your ZIP code is 89130. If the agent asks about payments, you remember paying part of it with your card when you signed back up, and that a couple of days later your bank's bill-pay also sent the region a payment you had set up before you knew the card had gone through, but you cannot recall the amounts and you say the agent should go by the account. If the agent tells you that something on your old Prime enrollment has to be settled first, or that money will go back to your bank account or to the card you paid with, you say that is fine. If the agent tells you the payment is yours to authorize, you agree, and when the agent hands you the payment step you complete it for exactly the enrollment, charge and amount the agent gives you. You never ask for anything beyond paying up your new Prime enrollment. Once the agent tells you your payment has gone through, you thank them and end the call.

Basis: 'its coverage period runs from the first to the last counted month that earlier credits did not cover'; counted months are April, May and June (Select coverage, from April through August, reaches every month of Q2), and the earlier credit covers 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-30, so April is the only month left.

edges.condition: Every month from the month containing the enrollment's effective date through the last month its first installment owes lies inside the coverage period of a prime_fee_charge row on the enrollment's fee ledger.
edges.policy_source: An initial payment toward a new enrollment is figured only after the enrollment's installment charges cover every month from the month containing its effective date through the last month its first installment owes.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The new enrollment's application (2026-10-06) came after the August installment period ended, so its first installment runs through October, but the charges on its account cover only 2026-08-24 to 2026-08-31 and 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31; September lies inside no charge's coverage.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The supplement posted at step 13 covers 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30, so every month from August through October lies inside a charge's coverage, and the charges the initial payment settles total 81.03.

edges.condition: The payments posted against the new enrollment's first installment charge, less the refunds issued against them, do not exceed the installment's value plus the regular installments the duplicate-refund rule lets the region keep on the account.
edges.policy_source: An initial payment toward a new enrollment is figured only after its first installment carries no payments beyond its value other than what the region keeps on the account for the installments that follow.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The new enrollment's first installment (32.51) carries 90.00 of payments - 20.00 by recurring card on 2026-10-06 and 70.00 by bill-pay transfer on 2026-10-08 - with no refund against them, 57.49 beyond its value and more than the one regular installment (32.51) the region keeps while the card has collected.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The refund of 24.98 posted at step 11 against the transfer leaves 32.51 beyond the value, exactly the one regular installment the region keeps, and the refunds the initial payment owes again rise to 24.98.

edges.condition: Every month of the ended enrollment's last paid installment that the beneficiary's TRICARE Select enrollment coverage reaches (from the month containing its effective date through the month containing its disenrollment date, or every month from its effective month on where it has none), or that falls after the month containing the disenrollment date, lies inside the coverage period of a prime_fee_credit row against that installment.
edges.policy_source: An initial payment toward a new Prime enrollment is not taken until every month of the last paid installment of a Prime enrollment the beneficiary ended earlier in the same plan year that a following TRICARE Select enrollment's coverage reaches, or that falls after the month containing its disenrollment date, stands credited.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Raymond's TRICARE Select coverage (2026-04-17 to 2026-08-23) reaches April, a month of the ended enrollment's paid Q2 installment, but the only credit against Q2 covers 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-30; April stands uncredited.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The April credit posted at step 9 covers 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-30, so April, May and June of the Q2 installment all stand credited.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisites are parallel and commute: the credit reads only the ended enrollment's account and the Select enrollment; the duplicate refund reads the new first installment's payments, the arrangement's method and the card's collections, none of which the credit or the supplement touches; the supplement reads the new enrollment's charges and the Select records, no payment or refund. A run of all six orders of the three writes before the payment gave the same values in every order (credit 32.51, duplicate refund 24.98, supplement 16.01, initial payment 48.52) and one terminal DB hash; every declared factor of each write keeps its weight in every order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the supplement the charges the initial payment settles total the August and October charges, 65.02: payment 32.51 (65.02 - 90.00 + 24.98 + 32.51 ahead) instead of 48.52, and no supplement charge exists in the terminal state.
Without the refund nothing is owed again: payment 32.51 (81.03 - 90.00 + 0.00 + 32.51 ahead) instead of 48.52, and the refund row is missing from the terminal state.

State gate: without the April credit the ended enrollment's Q2 installment stands uncredited for April, so under the charter the initial payment may not be taken; the payment's own figure does not move (48.52, it reads only the new enrollment's account), and the credit row is missing and the ended enrollment's balance differs in the terminal state.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona states only the surface request - paying up the new Prime enrollment by a one-time payment from his checking account - and never mentions a supplement, a missing credit, the old enrollment or a refund. Its only references to other matters are passive: if asked about payments it recalls paying part by card when signing up and a bank bill-pay sent a couple of days later, but no amounts; if told the old enrollment must be settled first or that money goes back to his bank account or card it accepts; when handed the payment step it completes it as given.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: None of the four tools reads a status, a balance or another posting to decide whether to act: post_unused_month_credit_3ad1a050 creates the credit with the arguments given and lowers the balance; refund_first_installment_duplicate_7d2e91c4 copies the method of the named payment, creates the refund and raises the balance; post_first_installment_supplement_bc87e2fc creates the charge and raises the balance; pay_first_installment_by_bank_draft_5f63627f creates the payment. Each succeeds with any arguments, so a payment taken before the supplement, the refund or the April credit is written faithfully and simply lands a different terminal state.
